plan: Store the constructor's data dict as a private deep copy; to_data() returns another deep copy so callers can never alias internal state.
Provide a single depth-first generator over all items; total_word_count() and unresolved_markers() are folds over it, keeping traversal logic in one place.
Count note words by first deleting marker tokens matching \[\[\?(\w+)\]\] then counting \b\w+\b runs; references add their declared word_count.
Collect marker identifiers from note-text matches and from reference 'unresolved' lists into a set, returned sorted.
Render outline() with a recursive walk carrying a nesting level: title line unindented, each item at two spaces per level as '<kind>: <title>'.

Implement move() as validate-then-mutate: resolve item and its parent list, resolve destination list ('workspace' literal or a section/group id), reject non-string ids, missing ids, non-containers, self/descendant destinations (identity walk of the moved subtree), and out-of-range indices — all before touching the tree, so any ValueError leaves the data unchanged.
Detach by identity from the source list, then append (index=None) or insert at the validated index.
Include an in-memory unittest suite exercising counts, markers, outline, valid moves, and every rejection path with an unchanged-snapshot assertion.
mechanisms: single deep-copied internal tree with defensive-copy export
shared depth-first item generator feeding both aggregations
marker-stripping regex pass before word tokenization
set-union marker collection with lexicographic sort
full pre-validation of move (existence, string ids, containership, cycle check by subtree identity walk, insertion-index bounds) before any mutation
